sections.heading: Recognition and inclusion
paragraphs: The Press Information Bureau records the Prime Minister’s congratulation to Ravanni Valasanini for winning bronze at the Asian Para Games. Such recognition can make para-athletic achievement more visible and help contest assumptions that disability limits excellence.

The practical mechanism is social and institutional attention: visibility can encourage participation and motivate public bodies to treat accessibility and sporting opportunity as inclusion concerns. However, recognition itself does not prove that those conditions exist.

sections.heading: From praise to opportunity
paragraphs: A complete inclusion framework would ask whether athletes can access facilities, trained coaches, equipment, travel support, competition exposure and protection from discrimination. These are analytical dimensions, not facts established by the supplied record.

The key limitation is evidentiary: the official summary gives no event-specific details, classification, performance data or information on policy support. UPSC answers should therefore distinguish the confirmed congratulation from broader recommendations.
